records.cause: Apple blamed an internal update. It did not identify the specific change.

records.quote: Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning.

records.summary: A technology issue affected United departures. The airline said airborne flights and United Express flights continued unaffected.
records.rationale: United said it saw no indication of a cybersecurity issue. Its statement did not establish a final root cause.
records.cause: United attributed the delays to a technology issue. Pilots described trouble with software used for final aircraft weight checks before takeoff.
records.speaker: United Airlines, via Associated Press

records.title: Software bug slows bank transactions
records.summary: Chase said a hardware-system software bug slowed some transactions and customer service. Other banks could see delayed receipts from Chase.
records.rationale: Spokesperson Joe Evangelisti told AP the issue was not cyber-related. Chase traced the outage to a software bug affecting internal hardware.
records.cause: A software bug affected hardware systems operated by Chase. A delayed transfer from Chase could also appear as a problem at the receiving bank.
records.speaker: JPMorgan Chase, via The Wall Street Journal
records.quote: there is no evidence this is cyber-related

history.text: Chase attributed transaction delays to a software bug. The New York Times reported that normal operations resumed.
Follow-up reporting distinguished delays involving Chase from independent bank outages.

records.title: Communications failure halts U.S. departures
records.summary: The FAA stopped departures across the United States after its communications and radar feeds became unstable. Flights resumed that evening.
records.rationale: The FAA traced the disruption to excess network traffic. On Nov 17, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said investigators still could not explain why the router failure had such wide effects.
records.cause: Excess traffic destabilized legacy equipment during telecom work. The FAA said the network stabilized after its contractor isolated two sites.
records.speaker: Federal Aviation Administration · Nov 15
records.quote: Based on all available evidence, we have no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor.

history.text: The FAA reported instability around 3:30 p.m. Eastern and ordered a nationwide ground stop.
Air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. Eastern on Nov 13.
The FAA published its initial technical findings and said it had no indication of an attack.
The FAA temporarily paused related router installations.
Duffy said investigators still did not know why a router failure could disrupt so much of the network.

records.impactNote: The FAA halted departures nationwide. Flights already in the air could land.
records.assessment: The FAA reported no indication of an attack. The root cause remains open.

denial.speaker: Federal Aviation Administration
denial.quote: Based on all available evidence, we have no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor.
denial.note: The secretary also described the failure as internal on ABC, while explicitly allowing for a later FBI finding. The agency’s written assessment is qualified.

records.title: Network change sends Outlook and Teams offline
records.summary: Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, and Copilot experienced a widespread disruption across multiple regions.
records.rationale: Microsoft’s Charles Lamanna explicitly ruled out a cyberattack and AI tooling.
records.cause: Microsoft traced the problem to a prior network-capacity upgrade that surfaced after a subsequent change. Cascading failures and a rush of simultaneous requests made recovery harder.
records.speaker: Charles Lamanna, Microsoft executive vice president, on X
records.quote: This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling.

records.title: Hospital network failure postpones operations
records.summary: A network failure disrupted phones and IT services at the Brussels university hospital. Planned operations were postponed.
records.rationale: The hospital initially reported no indication of an attack. Its next-day statement ruled one out and said it had detected no data leak.
records.cause: Network failure. The hospital declined to identify the component that failed.
records.speaker: UZ Brussel · Dutch-language statement
records.quote: Er is geen sprake van een cyberaanval en er werd geen datalek vastgesteld.

history.text: The hospital postponed planned operations after the network failed.
The hospital resumed normal operations and explicitly ruled out a cyberattack.

records.impactNote: The hospital’s phones and IT systems were disrupted. Operations were postponed and partner hospitals also restored systems.
records.assessment: The hospital explicitly ruled out a cyberattack.

denial.speaker: UZ Brussel
denial.quote: Er is geen sprake van een cyberaanval en er werd geen datalek vastgesteld.
denial.translation: There was no cyberattack, and no data leak was found.

records.title: Second nationwide standalone 5G outage in Japan
records.assessment: Docomo found no signs of a cyberattack.
records.summary: Calls, mobile data and texts were unreliable for standalone 5G subscribers on November 16. Docomo restored service after nearly six hours.
records.cause: Docomo attributed the November 16 outage to traffic concentrating on switching equipment for its standalone 5G subscribers.
records.speaker: NTT Docomo, November 16 service notice (Japanese)
records.quote: 不正アクセスの形跡やサイバー攻撃を示す事象は確認されておりません。
records.rationale: The operator said it found no signs of unauthorized access or a cyberattack in its checks. Its wording describes the evidence available at the time.
records.impactNote: Calls, data and texts were affected for standalone 5G subscribers across Japan. Emergency calls, 4G and other 5G subscribers were unaffected.

denial.speaker: NTT Docomo
denial.quote: 不正アクセスの形跡やサイバー攻撃を示す事象は確認されておりません。
denial.translation: Investigators have found no signs of unauthorized access or indications of a cyberattack.

records.assessment: Marriott’s review found no sign of a cyber cause.
records.rationale: Marriott gave AP and Skift its review finding. It described a technical issue and did not publicly identify a failed component.
records.cause: Technical issue affecting authentication on Marriott.com and the Bonvoy app.
records.speaker: Marriott spokesperson, in an email to AP

records.title: Standalone 5G disruption affects calls, data and texts across Japan
records.summary: Docomo’s standalone 5G service was disrupted for 8 hours and 43 minutes. The operator said it found congestion in a switch serving those subscribers.
records.cause: Congestion at a switching system serving standalone 5G customers.
records.assessment: Docomo found no signs of a cyberattack in its investigation.
records.speaker: NTT Docomo
records.quote: 不正アクセスの形跡やサイバー攻撃を示す事象は確認されておりません。
records.rationale: The operator’s bulletin says it had found no evidence of unauthorized access or a cyberattack. Its restoration notice identified switch congestion as the operational cause.
records.impactNote: Calls, data and texts were affected for standalone 5G subscribers nationwide. Emergency calling, 4G and other 5G services remained available.

denial.speaker: NTT Docomo
denial.quote: 不正アクセスの形跡やサイバー攻撃を示す事象は確認されておりません。
